mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in consumer demand (GDPC1) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as rising demand boosts corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window or 20-day returns in rising demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate crosses above 2.0% from below, signaling monetary tightening, S&P 500 forward returns are expected to decline over the next 20 days due to higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not decline significantly when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0%, or the signal is a false positive in a non-tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising Federal Funds Rates (monetary tightening) and falling Unemployment Rates (labor costs) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days, reflecting contractionary policies.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% and UNRATE falls below 9.5%
regime_hint: monetary tightening with falling labor costs
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative despite the trigger, or the combination of FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not align with contractionary expectations.

mechanism_narrative: An upward crossing of the Industrial Production Index above 105.0 (indicating strong supply growth) triggers positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as production capacity expands.
failure_condition: INDPRO crosses above 105 but 20-day returns are not positive, or the surge is temporary without sustained supply growth.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime with CPIAUCSL below 2.0% and rising demand (GDPC1), S&P 500 forward returns are expected to be positive over 20 days due to low inflation and strong demand.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL <2.0 and GDPC1 is rising, or the regime conditions are not met.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand (HOUST) surges above 680 and monetary policy (FEDFUNDS) eases (falls below 1.5%), S&P 500 returns are predicted to rise over 20 days as demand outpaces tight money.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 680 and FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5%
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not rise when HOUST and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger, or the combination does not reflect demand outpacing easing.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in labor demand (HOUST) above 680 triggers positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as increased hiring signals economic growth.
failure_condition: HOUST crosses above 680 but 20-day returns are not positive, or the surge is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in Industrial Production (INDPRO) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as expanding supply boosts corporate profits and market confidence.
failure_condition: INDPRO trend reverses or 60-day returns are not positive despite sustained supply growth.
